title: Accurate gap control of 3D-integrated superconducting quantum circuits using asymmetric indium architecture and multi-angle flip-chip bonding
authors: L. Richard, N. Bruckmoser, J. Feigl, D. Bunch, A. Bhattacharjee, L. Koch, I. Tsitsilin, V. P. Bader, H. Hu, L. Södergren, S. Filipp
abstract: Flip-chip 3D integration is a key enabling technology for overcoming the routing and layout constraints of planar superconducting quantum processors, but it requires accurate and uniform control of the inter-chip spacing while preserving qubit coherence. In conventional processes, thick indium bumps are deposited symmetrically on both chips, while dedicated spacers are introduced to limit the residual tilt. Here, we present a flip-chip bonding process based on an asymmetric indium architecture, combining $20\,μ\mathrm{m}$ thick indium bumps on the control chip with $200\,\mathrm{nm}$ thin indium pads on the qubit chip. Using electrical and microwave measurements, we demonstrate low resistance and low loss indium interconnects, and show that transmon qubits integrated with this process reach relaxation and coherence times of $T_1=(159\pm14)\,μ\mathrm{s}$ and $T_{\mathrm{2,echo}}=(294\pm42)\,μ\mathrm{s}$, respectively, comparable to planar devices. Combined with a multi angle compression procedure that suppresses systematic tilt, this approach reduces the average post bonding tilt to $(20\pm12)\,μ\mathrm{rad}$. These results establish an asymmetric indium architecture combined with multi angle compression as a robust, coherence preserving route toward 3D integrated superconducting quantum processors.
summary: This paper presents a breakthrough method for 3D integrating superconducting quantum circuits using an asymmetric indium bonding architecture combined with multi-angle compression. This technique solves the critical issues of maintaining precise inter-chip spacing and minimizing systematic tilt, leading to high-coherence transmon qubits comparable to planar devices.
main_problem: The primary challenge is achieving accurate and uniform control of inter-chip spacing in 3D-integrated superconducting quantum circuits while maintaining high qubit coherence.
main_result: The combination of an asymmetric indium architecture and a multi-angle flip-chip bonding procedure successfully established a robust method, yielding transmon qubits with coherence times comparable to planar devices.
method: The authors employed a novel bonding technique involving asymmetric indium pads and a multi-angle compression procedure to minimize systematic tilt during 3D integration.
model_or_system: The research focuses on superconducting quantum processors utilizing transmon qubits integrated via flip-chip 3D bonding. The system involves a control chip and a qubit chip connected by indium interconnects.
key_observables: Relaxation time ($T_1$), echo coherence time ($T_{2,echo}$), average post-bonding tilt angle, and inter-chip spacing standard deviation.
important_parameters: Indium bump thickness (20 $\mu$m vs 200 nm), target spacing ($\approx 10 \mu$m), and residual tilt ($\approx 20 \mu$rad).
main_assumptions: Conventional bonding methods are limited by residual contamination or systematic tilt, necessitating the proposed asymmetric and multi-angle approach.
figures_summary: Figures compare three bonding approaches (single-bond, spacers only, multi-angle) showing improvements in spacing uniformity and reduction of systematic tilt angles.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first identifying the limitations of current 3D bonding techniques, then detailing the asymmetric architecture and multi-angle bonding process, followed by comprehensive electrical and microwave characterization of the resulting quantum circuits.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses hardware limitations in scaling quantum processors, which is crucial for realizing fault-tolerant quantum computation architectures.
